project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas family-first recognition module centered on Juncus vs Luzula and sedge/grass separation
project_scope.note: The project pool contains Juncus and Luzula. The lesson emphasizes visible 6-tepal flowers and capsule fruit rather than the oversimplified 'rushes are round' mnemonic.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Find an individual flower. Juncaceae flowers usually look like tiny six-pointed brown/green flowers: 6 persistent tepals, usually 3 or 6 stamens, and a superior ovary that matures into a capsule.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Mostly perennial herbs with basal leaves; culms can be round or flattened. Leaves have sheaths and blades that may be flat, channeled or round.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually bisexual and radially symmetric with 6 similar tepals in two whorls. Stamens usually 3 or 6. Ovary superior, 1- or 3-locular.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A loculicidal capsule with 3 to many seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: If the plant looks sedge-like but you can clearly see little 6-tepal flowers and a many-seeded capsule, move to Juncaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole rush → flower with 6 tepals → capsule → Juncus/Luzula split → sedge/grass comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Rushes stop looking like featureless green stems once you zoom into the flower. Six tepals and a capsule are the family door.

steps.title: 1 · Zoom into a real rush flower
steps.look_for: Tiny star-like flowers with 6 narrow tepals that persist around the developing fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: This immediately separates a rush flower from a sedge spikelet or a grass floret.

steps.title: 2 · Follow the flower to a capsule
steps.look_for: A dry capsule inside the six tepals, with several seeds rather than one sedge nutlet.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit is one of the strongest family-level tie-breakers against Cyperaceae.

steps.title: 3 · Juncus door
steps.look_for: Leaves generally glabrous; sheaths open; capsules 1- or 3-chambered with many seeds.
steps.why_it_matters: Juncus accounts for most rush diversity in the project pool.

steps.title: 4 · Luzula door
steps.look_for: Woodrush leaves generally have conspicuous hairs along the margins; the one-chambered capsule normally contains three seeds.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the clean family-internal split from Juncus.

comparisons.title: Juncaceae vs Cyperaceae
comparisons.rule: Rush: 6 persistent tepals + capsule with several seeds. Sedge: minute flower under a scale + one hard one-seeded nutlet/achene.

comparisons.title: Juncaceae vs Poaceae
comparisons.rule: Rushes lack the grass floret architecture of glumes, lemma and palea and usually lack conspicuous grass nodes/collar/ligule structure.

comparisons.title: Juncus vs Luzula
comparisons.rule: Juncus leaves generally glabrous and capsules many-seeded; Luzula usually has hairy leaf margins and a capsule with three seeds.

visual_lesson.caveat: Round stems are common in rushes but are not the family definition. Use flowers and fruit when possible.

genera.fast_cue: glabrous leaves/open sheaths + 6-tepal flower + many-seeded capsule
hairy leaf margins + 6-tepal flower + usually 3-seeded capsule

visual_targets.annotation_goal: show capsule opening and multiple seeds
